evidence_articles.content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday (April 5, 2026) said the philosophy of his party is that of the celebrated musician Zubeen Garg, who worked his entire life to unite Assam. Addressing an election rally in Assam's Biswanath district, he alleged that Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma is the "most corrupt CM" in India and action will be taken against him after the Congress forms a government in the State. "Zubeen Garg worked his entire life to unite people of Assam, he never misbehaved with anyone. The Congress philosophy is also like that, to spread love against hatred," Mr. Gandhi said. He alleged that the BJP government led by Sarma is spreading hatred against people and communities. "Let him speak for some more days. After that, the Congress will form government in Assam and legal action will follow even if he asks for forgiveness," Mr. Gandhi said. Published - April 05, 2026 02:26 pm IST

evidence_articles.content: Himanta Sarma expands Assam Cabinet, balances new faces and loyalists, groups and regions The 17-member Himanta Cabinet, which has 13 ministers from BJP and two and one from AGP and BPF respectively, continues to accommodate ex-Congress leaders who had followed Sarma into BJP The Himanta Cabinet has a few new faces, even as it continues to accommodate prominent former Congress leaders who had followed Sarma into the BJP some years ago. (Photo: Facebook/Himanta Biswa Sarma) Twelve new ministers took the oath of office in Assam Friday as Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma carried out his Cabinet expansion, taking the strength of his new ministry to 17. The Himanta Cabinet has a few new faces, even as it continues to accommodate prominent former Congress leaders who had followed Sarma into the BJP some years ago. The senior-most among these ex-Congress leaders in the Himanta ministry 2.0 is Ajanta Neog, who had been sworn in with Sarma last month. Pijush Hazarika and Jayanta Malla Baruah, both Sarma loyalists who were prominent members of his last ministry, were inducted into the Council of Ministers Friday. Both of them were first-time MLAs when they quit the Congress and joined the BJP soon after Sarma’s switch to the BJP in 2015, with both going on to become Cabinet ministers. One of the entrants into the Council of Ministers, Sushanta Borgohain, has a similar trajectory. He too was a first-time MLA with the Congress when Sarma left it, but he went on to remain with the party for another six years. In 2021, soon after he was elected on a Congress ticket, he defected to the BJP. He was subsequently elected from the same seat on a BJP ticket later that year. One of the new faces in the ministry is Biswajit Daimary, who was the Speaker in the previous Assembly. Daimary is the BJP’s senior-most leader from the Bodo community, which is Assam’s single largest tribal group. A former Rajya Sabha MP and a long-time member of the Bodoland People’s Front (BPF), he had joined the BJP in 2020, which gave the party a prominent face in the Bodoland region. Ranoj Pegu, who was the Minister of Education and Welfare of Plain Tribes & Backward Classes (non-BTC) in the previous Himanta-led government, has also been made a minister now. A former Chief Executive Member of the Mising Autonomous Council, Pegu is a prominent leader from the Mising community, another prominent tribal community in the state. Story continues below this ad However, the expanded Himanta ministry does not have representation from the Karbi and Dimasa tribes from the large hill districts of Central Assam. It includes two ministers from Southern Assam’s Barak Valley, Krishnendu Paul and Kaushik Rai, who were both ministers in the last BJP government. Ashwini Roy Sarkar, a leader from the Koch Rajbongshi community from Dhubri district, is a new entrant into the ministry. The other new Cabinet face, who was sworn in last month, is one of the BJP’s senior-most leaders in the state, Rameshwar Teli, a tea-tribe leader who had previously been Union Minister of State for Food Processing Industries and then handled the Petroleum and Natural Gas portfolio in the Narendra Modi-led NDA government at the Centre. Yet another new face in the Himanta Cabinet is first time MLA Nilima Devi, who has been elected from the Mangaldai seat. The president of the Assam Pradesh BJP Mahila Morcha, Nilima, and Ajanta Neog are the only women in the Cabinet. Story continues below this ad Other prominent faces from the previous Himanta ministry who were sworn in Friday include senior Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) leader Keshab Mahanta, who has joined his party colleague Atul Bora in the Cabinet. They also include Ashok Singhal, a senior BJP leader and a prominent member of the last ministry, who also courted controversies for his polarising posts on social media. Charan Boro, the BPF’s lone minister, had been sworn in last month with Sarma. The 17-member Himanta Cabinet has thus 13 BJP ministers with the party’s allies AGP and BPF having two ministers and one, respectively. recent_articles.title: Himanta Sarma expands Assam Cabinet, balances new faces and loyalists, groups and regions | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Sarma**, Assam's Chief Minister, expanded his cabinet to 17 members on Friday. The new ministers include several former Congress leaders who joined the BJP with **Sarma**, such as Ajanta Neog and Pijush Hazarika, along with Sushanta Borgohain, Biswajit Daimary, Ranoj Pegu, and Rameshwar Teli.  The cabinet also includes representatives from Southern Assam's Barak Valley and the Koch Rajbongshi community. The expansion reflects a balance between new faces and loyalists, while maintaining representation from various regions and communities within Assam.

recent_articles.title: Assam Cabinet undergoes expansion, 12 MLAs sworn in - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma** expanded his **Assam** cabinet on Friday, June 5th, 2026, with the swearing-in of 12 new ministers.  The newly sworn-in members include **BJP** MLAs Ranoj Pegu, Ashok Singhal, Biswajit Daimary and AGP's Keshab Mahanta. The cabinet now has a total of 17 members, including the Chief Minister.

recent_articles.title: 12 More Ministers To Be Part Of Himanta Sarma Cabinet, Oath Tomorrow
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Sarma**, the Chief Minister of Assam, announced his 12-member cabinet for a swearing-in ceremony on Friday. The new council will have 17 ministers, with two vacancies to be filled over the year.  The newly appointed ministers include Ashwini Ray Sarkar, Ashok Singhal, Bimal Borah, Biswajit Daimary, Jayanta Mallabaruah, Kaushik Rai, Keshab Mahanta, Krishnendu Paul, Nilima Devi, Pijush Hazarika, Ranoj Pegu, and Susanta Borgohain.  The swearing-in ceremony will formally constitute the new council under Sarma's leadership.

recent_articles.title: Assam’s Council of Ministers to be expanded on June 5 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, Chief Minister of Assam, announced the expansion of the state's Council of Ministers on June 5th.  The expansion will bring the total number of ministers to a maximum of 19, aligning with the constitutional limit of 15% of the Assembly seats. The decision follows Mr. Sarma's previous statement that the government would expand its ministerial team over time.  He did not specify the number of new ministers or their identities.

recent_articles.title: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Sarma To Expand Cabinet On June 5, 9 MLAs Likely To Be Inducted
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the Assam Chief Minister, announced that his cabinet will be expanded on June 5th. The expansion is expected to include eight to nine MLAs as Cabinet Ministers and two Ministers of State.  Political observers anticipate a mix of experienced leaders and new entrants from the BJP and its alliance partners. **Narendra Modi**, the Prime Minister, was among the senior leaders who attended Sarma's swearing-in ceremony on May 12th.

recent_articles.title: 'Done deal': CM Himanta Biswa Sarma on NDA seat-sharing for Assam polls - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** stated that the seat-sharing arrangement within the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** for the upcoming Assam assembly elections is finalized. The alliance includes the BJP, **Asom Gana Parishad (AGP)**, **United People's Party Liberal (UPPL)**, and the **Bodoland People's Front (BPF)**, along with other parties like **Rabha Hasong Joutha Sangram Samiti (RHJSS)** and **Janashakti Party (JP)**. Sarma confirmed that after the completion of all processes, the state leadership will meet **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** to present a list of probable candidates.  The elections are expected in March-April following the delimitation exercise in 2023.

recent_articles.title: Fast-track court frames charges against seven accused in Zubeen Garg death case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Zubeen Garg**, the renowned cultural icon, was found dead in Singapore in September 2025. **Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** stated that Garg’s death was a result of a conspiracy, while a Singapore coroner's inquiry concluded it was an accidental drowning.  A special fast-track court on Tuesday (May 26, 2026) framed charges against seven accused, including **Shyamkanu Mahanta**, the event organizer, and **Siddharth Sharma**, Garg’s manager, for murder. The trial is scheduled to begin on June 8th.

recent_articles.title: UCC implementation in Assam: Muslim organisations seek consultations with government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Muslim religious and social organizations** in Assam have urged the **Assam government** to consult with them before implementing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC). The organizations, including factions of Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind, Jamaat-e-Islami, Ahle Sunnat, Muslim Personal Law Board, Nadwatul Tamir, Milli Council, and All Assam Minority Students’ Union, met to discuss their concerns. They emphasized the need for wider consultations before the proposed legislation is introduced, citing its direct impact on Islamic religious practices and personal laws. **Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** stated that the UCC would be tabled in the Assembly on May 26th, while also assuring that tribal communities under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution would be exempted from its purview.

recent_articles.title: BJP MLA Tapas Roy sworn in as Pro-tem Speaker of West Bengal Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tapas Roy**, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and MLA from Maniktala, was sworn in as the Pro-Tem Speaker of the West Bengal Assembly on Tuesday, May 12, 2026. **Suvendu Adhikari**, the Chief Minister, attended the ceremony. The oath-taking of other MLAs will be held on Wednesday and Thursday, with the election for Speaker scheduled for Friday.

recent_articles.title: Assam swearing-in LIVE: Himanta Biswa Sarma takes oath as Assam CM; Four MLAs sworn in as Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma** was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Assam for a second consecutive term on Tuesday, May 2, 2026. **Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya** administered the oath of office at a ceremony held at the Veterinary Ground in Guwahati.  Joining **Sarma** were four other MLAs who took oaths as Ministers: **Rameswar Teli**, **Ajanta Neog**, **Atul Bora**, and **Charan Boro**. The event was attended by prominent figures including **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, Nitin Gadkari, Sarbananda Sonowal, Pabitra Margherita**, and **BJP president Nitin Nabin**. This marks the formation of a third successive NDA government in the state.

recent_articles.title: NDA leaders stake claim to form Assam government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**-led **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)**, was unanimously elected as the leader of the Assam Legislature Party.  Following this, the NDA staked a claim to form the government in Assam with the support of 102 MLAs. The swearing-in ceremony for the new council of ministers is scheduled for May 12th. **J.P. Nadda**, Union Minister and central observer for the BJP Legislature Party meeting, announced that eight BJP legislators proposed Sarma's name as their leader.  The newly elected members of the BJP and its regional allies — **Asom Gana Parishad (AGP)** and **Bodoland People’s Front (BPF)** — chose their leaders in the morning.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet 2026: From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul, Ministers who were sworn in along with Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, newly sworn in as the Chief Minister of West Bengal, inducted five new ministers into his cabinet on Saturday. The swearing-in ceremony was attended by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Ministers Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, J. P. Nadda, and Dharmendra Pradhan**, among other BJP leaders.  **Dilip Ghosh**, a senior BJP leader who secured victory in the Kharagpur seat, **Agnimitra Paul**, a fashion designer-turned-legislator who won Asansol Dakshin, **Ashok Kirtania**, a BJP stalwart who gained victory in Bangaon Uttar, and **Kshudiram Tudu**, a former school teacher from Ranibandh (ST) constituency, were among the newly appointed ministers.  **Nisith Pramanik**, a key face of BJP from North Bengal, was also inducted into the cabinet.

recent_articles.title: Bangladesh failed to give ‘actionable response’ to diplomatic notes: India - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** has sent over 1,000 diplomatic notes and 456 "consolidated reminders" to **Bangladesh** since September 2020 regarding the repatriation of suspected illegal Bangladeshi immigrants.  The Indian government's note verbale, sent on April 30th after a Bangladesh protest against Assam's former Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's claims about border security, stated that no actionable response has been received.

recent_articles.title: ​Cost of success: On the BJP’s victory in Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the BJP's leader in Assam, is expected to be sworn in as Chief Minister after leading the party to victory.  Sarma, who previously served as a Congress leader, has been instrumental in reshaping the state's political landscape through organizational prowess and communal rhetoric. The BJP's landslide win has significantly altered power dynamics within the party nationally, with Sarma being perceived as close to **Amit Shah**, the Union Home Minister. However, the party's victory has also sparked concerns about its impact on Assam's social fabric, particularly its divisive policies towards Bengali-speaking Muslim communities.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 results LIVE: CEC orders immediate arrest of those involved in post-poll violence in West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar** directed authorities to arrest those responsible for post-poll violence and vandalism in West Bengal following the deaths of two people and the ransacking of party offices. **Trinamool Congress** leaders accused **Bharatiya Janta Party** workers of targeted attacks, while **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** sought support from the **Communist Party of India (CPI)** to form a government in Tamil Nadu.  **Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** is expected to meet with the Governor and submit his resignation, paving the way for a new government.

recent_articles.title: Assam elections 2026: How have smaller allies fared? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma** of the **BJP** led the North-East Democratic Alliance (NEDA) to victory in Assam's Assembly elections, securing a second term with 102 seats. The Congress-led alliance won only 21 seats, while the All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) and Trinamool Congress secured two and one seat respectively.  The BJP campaigned on issues of illegal immigration removal and infrastructure development.

recent_articles.title: Assam poll verdict rejection of blue blood politics: Himanta Biswa Sarma - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the **Chief Minister of Assam**, attributed the **BJP's** victory in the state elections to a rejection of "blue blood" politics, claiming that voters favored the party over candidates whose fathers held previous political positions.  The BJP secured 102 seats out of 126, while several Congress candidates, including Gaurav Gogoi, Debabrata Saikia, and Diganta Barman, lost their respective constituencies. Seven women were elected to the Assam Assembly, with a success rate of 11.86%.

recent_articles.title: ​Lost and found: The Hindu Editorial on the 2026 Assembly elections - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Assembly elections in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry resulted in significant shifts in India's political landscape. The BJP secured victories in Assam and Puducherry while the Congress suffered its worst performance in Assam. In West Bengal, the BJP capitalized on long-term planning and a tainted election process to achieve a decisive victory.  The TVK led by actor C. Joseph Vijay made a historic debut in Tamil Nadu, becoming the first non-Dravidian Chief Minister. The Congress faces an internal challenge in Kerala with multiple candidates vying for the Chief Minister position. **Amit Shah**, Home Minister, is likely to gain further influence within the BJP as it continues its expansion across regions and social groups.  The results suggest a potential realignment of the Opposition, opening opportunities for the Congress to consolidate and galvanize support against the BJP.

recent_articles.title: BJP-led NDA scores hat-trick in Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party** (BJP) secured a historic victory in the Assam Assembly elections, winning 102 of 126 seats to retain power for a third consecutive term. The BJP's regional allies, the **Asom Gana Parishad** (AGP) and the **Bodoland People’s Front** (BPF), also performed well, winning 10 and 10 seats respectively.  The Congress party suffered its worst performance since losing power in 2016, winning only 19 seats. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who retained his Jalukbari seat, is now considered one of the BJP's most prominent leaders in Assam.

recent_articles.title: Assam election results LIVE: Trends show NDA inching towards majority mark - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The counting of votes for the Assam Assembly elections began on Monday, May 4, 2026. **Election Commission of India** early trends show the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** leading in over 70 seats. The ruling NDA is seeking a third consecutive term while the Congress-led Opposition alliance hopes to regain power with the **Asom Sonmilito Morcha (ASM)**.  Counting is taking place at 40 centers across all 35 districts.

recent_articles.title: Bail order reminder that personal liberty can’t be sacrificed for political vendetta: Pawan Khera - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pawan Khera**, a Congress leader, was granted anticipatory bail by the **Supreme Court** after allegations were made against him regarding his comments on Assam Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma's** wife. The court found that the matter appeared to stem from political rivalry and granted pre-arrest bail with certain conditions.  **Abhishek Singhvi**, along with other legal representatives, defended Khera's liberty amidst threats and intimidation. The Congress hailed the decision as a victory for the rule of law, urging **Sarma** to reconsider his language and apologize.

recent_articles.title: Bangladesh's foreign ministry summons India's acting Envoy over Himanta’s remarks: report - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bangladesh's** Foreign Ministry summoned **India's** acting High Commissioner Pawan Badhe to lodge a formal protest over comments made by **Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma**.  **Ms. Ishrat Jahan**, Director General (South Asia), conveyed Bangladesh's displeasure with the remarks, which were deemed "disparaging" and undermining of bilateral relations. The official emphasized the need for restraint when addressing sensitive issues between the two countries.

recent_articles.title: Pawan Khera moves Supreme Court against denial of anticipatory bail - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pawan Khera**, leader of the **Congress**, challenged the **Gauhati High Court's** decision to deny him anticipatory bail in an FIR filed against him for allegedly making critical remarks about Assam Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma's** wife. The High Court rejected his plea, stating that custodial interrogation was necessary to uncover the source of his accusations.

recent_articles.title: Assam sees record voter turnout of over 85% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Assam** recorded its highest-ever voter turnout in the Assembly elections, with 85.62% of voters casting their ballots on Thursday (April 9, 2026).  The state witnessed largely peaceful voting despite reports of violence and allegations of proxy voting. **Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** hailed the historic turnout, attributing it to a desire to protect Assam's land, identity, and culture from illegal infiltration and demographic aggression. State Congress president **Gaurav Gogoi** thanked voters for their participation in the election, urging the Election Commission to ensure the security of EVMs and accurate vote counting on May 4th.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly election 2026 LIVE: Voting begins in 126 constituencies across the State; BJP eyes third term as Congress-led alliance mounts challenge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Assam** is holding its 126-member Assembly elections on April 9, 2026. The **BJP**, led by Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, is seeking a third consecutive term in power while the **Congress**, under the leadership of **Gaurav Gogoi**, aims to reclaim the state from the BJP. A total of 722 candidates are competing, including leaders like **Debabrata Saikia** and **Badruddin Ajmal**. Polling will take place across 31,490 polling stations in 35 districts.

recent_articles.title: ​Two plus one: On the April 9 Assembly elections in Kerala, Assam and Puducherry - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Public campaigning** for the April 9 Assembly elections in Kerala, Assam, and Puducherry concluded on Tuesday. Voting will take place in a single phase across all three regions on May 4th with results to be announced then. In Kerala, the incumbent **LDF**, led by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, is seeking a third consecutive term.  The **UDF** aims to capitalize on momentum gained in recent elections while the **CPI(M)** faces internal challenges and defections. In Assam, **Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** leads the BJP-led NDA campaign focused on Hindutva, welfare schemes, and anti-Muslim rhetoric. The **Congress** is countering with its own personalized campaign against Sarma's claims of links to Pakistan.  In Puducherry, an NDA government led by **N.

recent_articles.title: Assam Police team visits Khera’s Delhi residence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the **Assam Chief Minister**, declared that his police will pursue **Pawan Khera**, a Congress leader, to uncover those who provided him with allegedly forged documents tarnishing his family's reputation.  **Khera** has been accused of making false claims about **Riniki Bhuyan Sharma**, the wife of the CM, including allegations of foreign passports and shell companies. The Assam police have sought permission from Telangana authorities to investigate **Khera** after he was not found at his New Delhi residence.  The Congress party has requested investigations by the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** or **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** into the accusations.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly election 2026: Curtains down on high-voltage campaign - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly elections concluded on April 7, with voters casting their ballots for the state's 126 seats. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, and other BJP leaders campaigned against the opposition Congress, accusing it of promoting infiltrators and failing to address development issues. The Congress countered by highlighting corruption allegations against the ruling party and promising justice for singer Zubeen Garg if elected. Prominent candidates include Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Gaurav Gogoi (Congress), Badruddin Ajmal (AIUDF), and Debabrata Saikia (opposition).  The elections will be held in a single phase on April 9th.

recent_articles.title: Assam Police at Pawan Khera's residence in New Delhi; Himanta says Congress leader ‘ran away’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Assam** Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** accused the **Congress** party of a “foreign-influenced misinformation campaign” against him and his wife, Riniki Bhuyan Sarma.  Following an investigation into allegations made by **Pawan Khera**, a **Congress** leader, about Ms. Sarma's alleged foreign assets, an **Assam** Police team is questioning **Khera** at his Delhi residence. The **Delhi** police are assisting in the proceedings.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly elections 2026: Bid to woo new voters in CM Himanta’s long-time constituency Jalukbari - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the Chief Minister of Assam, filed his nomination papers for the upcoming Assembly elections in Jalukbari constituency.  He faces competition from **Bidisha Neog** of the Congress and **Dipika Das** of the Bhumi Adhikar Party. The delimitation exercise has shifted some areas within the constituency, but Sarma is expected to win with a comfortable margin. He has been actively campaigning in the area, focusing on development projects and community outreach.  The BJP is working hard to secure strong voter turnout in this region, particularly in Garigaon, where there has been significant improvement in infrastructure and social welfare schemes since the 2023 delimitation.

recent_articles.title: Assam election verdict hinges on parties reading the tea leaves right - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly election campaign is being heavily influenced by the tea tribe community, which comprises almost 20% of voters.  **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress**, promised daily wages of ₹450 and Scheduled Tribe status for six communities, including tea tribes, while **Hemant Soren**, Jharkhand Chief Minister, campaigned for a candidate from the **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)**, highlighting the lack of ST status for these communities in Assam.  The BJP is promising land rights to over 3.5 lakh families and raising minimum wages to ₹500. The JMM's entry into the race has complicated matters for both major parties, but its impact on the tea tribe vote remains uncertain.

recent_articles.title: ‘Erasure of CM’ from BPF’s posters raises eyebrows in Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bodoland People’s Front (BPF)** in Assam has been accused of erasing photos of Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma** from posters supporting its candidates, particularly in Muslim-dominated areas. Political commentator **Dhanjit Das** suggests this move is a strategic attempt to appease the Bodo tribal community and counter potential backlash from Muslims who felt betrayed by the alliance with the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**. The **United People’s Party Liberal (UPPL)**, a rival party, sees an opportunity to capitalize on these sentiments and potentially gain ground in the upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Congress petitions Election Commission to cancel Assam CM’s candidature over ‘undisclosed assets’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the Chief Minister of Assam, is facing a petition from the **Assam Congress** to cancel his candidacy for the upcoming Assembly election. The petition alleges that he failed to disclose his wife's alleged offshore assets in his affidavit, violating the Representation of the People Act, 1951. A delegation led by former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister **Bhupesh Baghel** submitted the complaint to the Assam Chief Electoral Officer.  Sarma denies the allegations.

recent_articles.title: Assam Election 2026: What BJP and Congress promise in their manifestos - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming Assam Legislative Assembly elections are scheduled for April 9, 2026, with the counting of votes taking place on May 4, 2026. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Congress are the main contenders in this election, promising various policies to address issues such as land rights, economic development, and social welfare.  **Nirmala Sitharaman**, Union Finance Minister, presented the BJP's "Sankalp Patra" which focuses on implementing a Uniform Civil Code, protecting land and heritage, and furthering its development agenda. **Rahul Gandhi**, Congress leader, released the party's "Raijor Istahar", or people's manifesto, promising Scheduled Tribe status for six communities, an Anti Corruption Commission, and a white paper on Assam finances.  The elections will involve around 2.50 crore registered voters across 31,486 polling stations.

recent_articles.title: Congress concocted allegations against my wife using false info from Pak social media group: Assam CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, Assam Chief Minister, accused the **Congress** of fabricating claims about his wife's multiple passports and Dubai properties to influence the upcoming elections. He alleged that these accusations originated from a Pakistani social media group and were part of a larger attempt by Pakistan to interfere in the polls.  Sarma stated that he has filed a complaint against **Pawan Khera**, a Congress spokesperson, for making false allegations.

recent_articles.title: ‘Some people are more native, but it’s a question of citizenship’: Hiren Gohain - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hiren Gohain**, a prominent Assam writer and activist, advocates for Opposition unity in the upcoming election.  He believes this alliance would be more beneficial to voters than individual parties. **Harekrishna Deka**, leader of the **Assam Nagorik Sanmilani**, a citizens' collective he founded, has been calling for judicial intervention against **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, Assam's Chief Minister, over alleged hate speeches.  The High Court hearing on these claims has been postponed to April 21st. Gohain also discusses the complexities of defining "indigenous Assamese" and the impact of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act on Assam's demographics. He believes that extremism does not bring about positive change and that violence will ultimately harm the people of Assam.

recent_articles.title: Campaigning for BJP, Manipur CM woos Assam Manipuris - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Yumnam Khemchand Singh**, Manipur Chief Minister, campaigned for the **BJP** in Assam's Cachar district on April 5th, 2026. He projected Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** as a protector of Manipur's boundary and **Himanta Biswa Sarma** as a friend to Manipuri people.  Singh urged voters to support the BJP-led government in Assam, highlighting the inclusion of Manipuri as an associate official language. The campaign saw the participation of seven Manipur BJP legislators and State BJP president A. Sharda Devi.

recent_articles.title: Congress alleges Sarma’s wife holds three passports, Dubai properties; Assam CM rejects claims - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leader Pawan Khera alleged that the wife of **Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma**, Riniki Bhuyan Sharma, possesses passports from three countries and owns properties in Dubai.  Sarma vehemently denied these claims, calling them "malicious, fabricated, and politically motivated lies." He vowed to take legal action against Khera and asserted that the allegations are baseless. **Home Minister Amit Shah** and **Election Commission of India** officials have been called upon to investigate the matter.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly polls: Like Zubeen Garg, Cong works to unite people, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress party**,  compared his party's philosophy to that of musician **Zubeen Garg**, who worked to unite Assam. He accused **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the current Chief Minister of Assam, of being the "most corrupt CM in India" and promised legal action against him after the Congress forms a government. Gandhi also alleged that the BJP government led by Sarma is spreading hatred against people and communities.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly election: Less than a week before polls, BJP shifts focuses to youth empowerment, floods - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** in Assam has shifted its election focus from infiltrators and identity politics to youth empowerment and flood mitigation. **Information Minister Pijush Hazarika**, seeking re-election, highlighted the government's achievements in job creation, skill development initiatives like the Chief Minister Flight program, and flood management efforts.  He emphasized a commitment to exceeding two lakh jobs in the next five years and investing over ₹18,000 crore in the Flood-Free Assam Mission. The party also acknowledged the concerns of Gen Z and Gen Alpha regarding the late singer **Zubeen Garg**, and pledged to address them as part of its new campaign strategy.

recent_articles.title: Pakistan jibes become central to BJP’s Assam poll narrative - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the Chief Minister of Assam, has criticized **Lurinjyoti Gogoi**, the AJP candidate for Guwahati Central constituency, for his alleged links to "anti-national" elements.  Sarma also attacked **Sujata Gurung Chowdhury**, Kunki Chowdhury's mother, for publicly supporting Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid, both accused in the 2020 Delhi riots case. The controversy has drawn attention to Pakistan as a topic of discussion in the Assam election. **Saadulla**, a former Prime Minister of Assam, is being used by the BJP to highlight alleged infiltration attempts into the state during his tenure.

recent_articles.title: ‘Miyas’ will be game-changers in Assam election, says AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Asaduddin Owaisi**, president of the **All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM)**, predicted a "community tsunami" in favor of the **All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF)** on April 9th's Assam Assembly elections.  He urged voters to support the AIUDF and its candidate Mohammed Badruddin Ajmal, stating that "Miya" Muslims would be the game-changers. Owaisi criticized **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the Assam Chief Minister, for his alleged use of "politics of hatred" against Muslims and blamed the Congress for the rise of the BJP in Assam.  He also asserted that the AIUDF was a collective political asset representing marginalized communities.

recent_articles.title: Himanta 'most corrupt CM' in India; Modi, Shah, Sarma running 'land ATM' in Assam: Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, **Congress** leader, accused **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the **Assam** Chief Minister, of running a "land ATM" with **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**.  He alleged that three corporate houses have been given 98,400 bighas of land in Assam.  Gandhi also promised to deliver justice for singer Zubeen Garg's death within 100 days if the Congress wins the upcoming election. He criticized the BJP's governance and pledged to decentralize power and protect tribal rights.

recent_articles.title: PM’s policies pushing country deeper into crisis, says Priyanka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra**, Congress leader, criticized **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** and **Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** for what she called "double-slavery" governance in Assam. She accused them of prioritizing personal gain over the well-being of the people and threatened to withhold or cancel beneficiary schemes if they did not attend rallies.  Vadra also promised justice for late singer Zubeen Garg, who died in Singapore, and vowed a Congress government would deliver within its first 100 days. The single-phase election will be held on April 9th with counting scheduled for May 4th.

recent_articles.title: Congress fuelled infiltration, changed Assam’s demography: Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister, criticized the **Congress** for allegedly encouraging infiltration and demographic changes in Assam. He claimed that the BJP-led government has stopped new infiltrators but needs more time to remove those already present. **Shah** asserted that the nine Muslim-majority districts were a result of Congress's policies and accused them of using immigrants as vote banks. He also criticized the **Congress** for opposing electoral roll revisions and vowed to deport all infiltrators.  He emphasized the BJP's achievements in Assam, including peace restoration and development, while highlighting the party's commitment to protecting jobs for youth.

recent_articles.title: Fast justice for Zubeen Garg among five Congress guarantees for Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, Congress president, promised **justice for Zubeen Garg** within 100 days if elected in Assam.  He also outlined other guarantees including ₹50,000 to women for business ventures and monthly cash transfers, ₹1,250 pension for senior citizens, ₹25 lakh cashless health cover for families, and land rights for 10 lakh indigenous people. **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, Assam's Chief Minister, claimed Garg's death was part of a conspiracy while a Singapore coroner ruled it an accidental drowning.

recent_articles.title: Amit Shah promises UCC in Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister, stated that the **BJP** would introduce the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in Assam if re-elected for a third consecutive term. The proposed UCC includes a provision to ban polygamy and aims to bring uniformity in civil laws and strengthen social reforms.  **Assam** previously passed an anti-polygamy bill in 2025, seen as a step towards implementing the UCC. **Uttarakhand** was the first state to implement the UCC in 2025.

recent_articles.title: Amit Shah says curbing ‘infiltration not enough’, every illegal immigrant must be deported from Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, stated that the BJP government has stopped "infiltration" in Assam over the past ten years, but emphasized that all illegal immigrants must be sent back. He accused **Rahul Gandhi** and the **Congress** of opposing electoral roll revisions to protect infiltrators.  **Shah** also criticized the Congress's handling of national security during its rule, claiming it encouraged terrorists from Pakistan. The upcoming Assam Assembly elections are scheduled for April 9th with counting on May 4th.

recent_articles.title: BJP to score hat-trick in Assam, to come to power for third term in row: Nitin Nabin - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitin Nabin**, national chief of the **BJP**, announced that the party will form its third consecutive government in Assam, led by Chief Minister **Himanta Biswa Sarma**.  He attributed the state's development to the BJP's leadership since 2016 under Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**.  **Mr. Nabin** criticized previous Congress governments for prioritizing vote bank politics over development.

recent_articles.title: NDA will retain power in Assam with more than 90 seats, says Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister and leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, stated that the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) is expected to win over 90 seats in the upcoming Assam Assembly election. The NDA comprises the BJP, Asom Gana Parishad (AGP), and Bodoland People’s Front, with the BJP contesting all 126 constituencies. Shah attributed the NDA's strong prospects to improved law-and-order, infrastructure development under Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, and a peaceful environment free of insurgency or extremism.

recent_articles.title: Assam candidate has 37 bank accounts, 32 vehicles - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sewli Mohilary**, the BPF candidate from Kokrajhar Assembly constituency, declared total assets worth ₹54.04 crore, including 37 bank accounts and 16 tipper trucks.  Her husband, **Hagrama Mohilary**, the Bodoland Territorial Council chief, has significantly less wealth compared to her. **Mohammed Badruddin Ajmal**, the AIUDF chief, holds the highest assets at ₹222.34 crore, with a significant portion of his wealth in movable assets.  **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the BJP candidate for Jalukbari, and his wife, Riniki Bhuyan Sarma, reported a combined income of ₹35.16 crore in 2026, while **Gaurav Gogoi**, the Assam Congress president, and his wife Elizabeth Colburn Gogoi saw their combined income jump to ₹7.57 crore.

recent_articles.title: Singapore report ignites Zubeen death issue in Assam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A Singapore coroner's inquiry concluded that **Zubeen Garg**, the Assamese cultural icon, drowned accidentally.  **Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** maintains his belief that Garg was murdered, citing evidence of alcohol consumption and a conspiracy involving his co-singer, **Amritprabha Mahanta**. However, **Gaurav Gogoi**, the Congress president, challenged the Chief Minister's claim, arguing that the Singapore ruling contradicts his murder theory.  The differing findings have sparked debate about the investigation's validity.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly Elections: Voting trends and vote share since 2011 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Assam Assembly Elections are shaping up to be a high-stakes battle between the ruling BJP-led alliance, led by Himanta Biswa Sarma, and opposition parties like the Congress.  Since 2011, Assam has seen dramatic political shifts with the BJP's rise in 2016 and its subsequent retention of power in 2021. The state witnessed a landslide victory for the Congress in 2011, followed by the BJP's first win in the northeast region.  The upcoming elections will be closely watched as they could determine the future political landscape of Assam.

recent_articles.title: Harvesting anxiety: On Assam, its Assembly election - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **BJP** is seeking a third consecutive term in Assam's Assembly elections on April 9, 2026, while the **Congress** aims to regain power after a decade. The party's strategy focuses on communal mobilization and welfare schemes, but faces competition from regional parties like the **AIUDF**, the **Raijor Dal**, and the **AJP**.  The delimitation of constituencies in 2023 has impacted voter representation, creating a unique political landscape for the upcoming election.

recent_articles.title: Assembly election dates 2026 master guide: Dates for Assam, West Bengal, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Assembly elections will be held in four states and one Union Territory, with a total of 824 constituencies. The Election Commission has assumed responsibility for the Model Code of Conduct, which took effect immediately after the election dates were announced.  **BJP**, **Congress**, **AIUDF**, **UPPL**, **Mamata Banerjee**, **Suvendu Adhikari**, and **Sarbananda Sonowal** are among the key figures involved in the upcoming elections.  The voting process will involve 2.18 lakh polling booths and approximately 2.5 million election officials. The schedule for each state is as follows: Assam, West Bengal, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Puducherry.

recent_articles.title: Himanta, Assam BJP chief Dilip Saikia reach out to leaders threatening to contest as Independents - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several sitting MLAs and aspirants in Assam have threatened to contest as Independents after being denied BJP tickets for the upcoming assembly elections. **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, Chief Minister, and **Dilip Saikia**, State party chief, are attempting to appease these disgruntled leaders.  **Jayanta Das**, a senior party leader who was a probable candidate in Dispur, has publicly accused Sarma of making the party a "Congress BJP" by bringing in his close associates. Other veteran leaders like **Siddhartha Bhattacharya**, **Ramendra Narayan Kalita**, and **Atul Bora** have also expressed discontent over their denial of tickets. The BJP claims that these decisions are based on the delimitation exercise of 2023 and prioritizes fresh blood who worked hard for the party's growth at the grassroots level.

recent_articles.title: Assembly election LIVE: 116 candidates, including CM, Speaker, LoP file nominations in Assam till Friday - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma** and 116 other candidates filed their nomination papers for the Assam Assembly elections, which will be held on April 9, 2026.  The **TMC** released its manifesto for the West Bengal Assembly elections, focusing on welfare expansion and targeted social schemes. The first phase of voting in West Bengal is scheduled for April 23, 2026.

recent_articles.title: Assam CM, regional party chiefs file nominations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the **Assam Chief Minister**, and presidents of two non-NDA regional parties filed their nomination papers for the upcoming Assam Assembly elections.  Sarma is seeking election from Jalukbari, while **Pramod Boro**, president of the United People’s Party Liberal (UPPL), submitted his papers for Tamulpur. The Raijor Dal's **Akhil Gogoi** also filed his nomination for Sibsagar.  The Congress party and Raijor Dal entered into a seat-sharing deal, with Gaurav Gogoi stating their goal is to "build a new 'Bor Asom'" while the Raijor Dal president promised land rights for all if they form the government.

recent_articles.title: Assam polls: Congress, Raijor Dal seal seat-sharing deal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** and the **Raijor Dal** reached a seat-sharing agreement on Thursday, March 19, 2026, forming a six-party opposition bloc. The deal includes **Raijor Dal** contesting 13 seats, including its president's, and a "friendly contest" in two constituencies with **Congress**.  The agreement comes after weeks of negotiations and aims to challenge the ruling **BJP** in Assam's upcoming Assembly elections on April 9th.

recent_articles.title: Assam Congress weighs MP’s flight to BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pradyut Bordoloi**, a Congress MP from Assam, resigned and joined the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** in New Delhi on Wednesday.  He was accompanied by **Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** and **State BJP president Dilip Saikia**.  Congress leader **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra** expressed disappointment over Bordoloi's resignation, while **Jitendra Singh**, an AICC secretary in charge of Assam, suggested that the MP had been planning to join the BJP for a long time.  The Congress is facing internal dissent as several leaders are contemplating leaving the party ahead of the upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Assam polls: BJP keeps tribal council-based ally in limbo - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The BJP** has kept the **United People’s Party Liberal (UPPL)** in suspense about its status in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ahead of the 2026 Assam Assembly elections.  **Raju Kumar Narzary**, UPPL general secretary, wrote to **Dilip Saikia**, State BJP president, seeking clarity on their alliance status. The BPF, a previous ally, is now being considered for a larger share of seats in the upcoming election.
